title: Redundant controllers with a network reference point (NRP failure detector): can both be in charge?
source: Algorithm: B. Johansson, M. Ragberger, A. V. Papadopoulos, T. Nolte, 'Consistency Before Availability: Network Reference Point based Failure Detection for Controller Redundancy', IEEE ETFA 2023 (the backup of every cell is its Algorithm 3, --promote-rule takeover). Models and scenarios: B. Johansson, B. Pourvatan, Z. Moezkarimi, A. Papadopoulos, M. Sirjani, 'Formal Verification of Consistency for Systems with Redundant Controllers', MARS 2024, EPTCS 399, pp. 169-191 (Timed Rebeca models NRPFD.rebeca and LeasingNRPFD.rebeca, Table 1 cases 7 and 8, the leasing fix, Appendix C). Failure spacing: M. Sirjani et al., 'Actors for Timing Analysis of Distributed Redundant Controllers', Gul Agha Festschrift, LNCS 16120, Springer 2025 (a different node, its Eq. 5 and Eq. 6 are not reproduced here). Timing constants: one hop is Rebeca's networkDelay = 1 (the default L = U = 1, sd = 0); the round length H = 20U and the answer wait P = 10U are the defaults the source takes from the GulFest file. The timing rules of the regimes C, E and F are this example's own measurements on its Rust model of the MARS node (source header, runs of 2026-09-16), not published bounds.
property: NoDualPrimary, verbatim from NRPFD.property (!(DCN1Primary && DCN2Primary)): there is no instant, same-instant orders included, at which both controllers are PRIMARY. The monitor (the main thread) replays the role reports and asserts it once per execution, at the end, after both controllers have drained their channels (source line 1205).
citable_note: The 2026-09-18 audit lists this example (B01) as citable after the --promote-rule fidelity fix, and the current source has that fix. Caveats that are newer than the audit: (1) since every send is lossy (2026-09-30) both sides are dominated by blocked executions produced by the harness guard (timed self test at R = 4: 1 complete execution against 51,806 blocked), so quote verdicts, violating executions and wall times, and present the explored ratio as search cost, not as behaviours checked; (2) the boundaries are measured at a few points each on this model, they are not published bounds, and the lease-not-enough scenario (regimes F1, F2) is new and not cross-checked in Afra; (3) most baseline sides stop at their first violation and carry no count.
config_timed: build_config, source lines 1116-1129: Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().with_progress_report(usize::MAX) (line 1117); with_keep_going_after_error(true) only when --keep-going is given (lines 1118-1120); then .with_timed(L, U, sd).with_node_sd(main thread, 0).build() (lines 1124-1127). So: consistency model FIFO (library default, never set), every send lossy, storage lifetime sd at every thread except 0 at the monitor, scheduling policy LTR (library default), no parallel option (1 core per run). Every send gives its own transit bounds with send_msg_timed (lines 766-776): [L, U] for a DCN1 to switch hop, [3L, 3U] for a switch to DCN2 leg, exact [d, d] for timers, failure notices and role reports; every receive is the blocking recv_msg_block_timed (line 782). In the v9 cells (L, U, sd) is (1, 1, 0), (1, 2, 0) or (0, 1, 0).
config_baseline: build_config, source lines 1116-1122: Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().with_progress_report(usize::MAX), with_keep_going_after_error(true) only when --keep-going is given, then .build(): no clock (the transit bounds of send_msg_timed, the storage lifetime and the monitor override are ignored), consistency model FIFO (library default), every send lossy, scheduling policy LTR (library default), no parallel option (1 core per run).
program_differs_between_modes: no: the mode is read only in build_config (lines 1121-1128) and for the label of the summary line; the same send_msg_timed and recv_msg_block_timed calls run in both modes and their timing information is ignored without the clock
failing_tasks: Only the main thread (the monitor) asserts: traceforge::assert(!dual) at source line 1205. Under keep-going every violating execution prints the line main-thread-ThreadId(1) (checked with a local run). No controller or switch thread asserts, so no task-N line is expected. The panics at lines 774, 957, 994, 1102 and 1182 (unexpected message, unknown actor) are harness sanity checks; no v9 run ended with an error. The assume at line 784 (sequence check of the harness guard) blocks an execution, it is not an assertion.

counters.meaning: executions in which the monitor saw both controllers PRIMARY at some instant (the DUAL_PRIMARY static, bumped once per execution just before the assertion, line 1202). Equal to the violating executions of the tool on every finished v9 run. Not printed when the run stops at the first violation (the binary panics before the summary line).
the same static as violations, printed twice in the summary line

executions in which the monitor reached the end with every channel drained (no lost and no skipped message). completed = execs + violations, because a violating execution is aborted by the assertion and filed under blocked
times DCN1 gave up being primary (at most once per execution); stepdowns = completed means DCN1 was fully isolated in every execution
times DCN2 took over (at most once per execution), by the shortcut or after an answered takeover question
promotions made by the shortcut (both counts over the limit in the same round, variant nrp only)
questions the backup sent to the landmark because both of its counts were over the limit
landmark answers the backup read; 0 in a leasing cell means the lease was never consulted
landmark answers that said a primary question came just before, which puts the backup's lease count back to zero (variant leasing)

completed executions in which the backup read at least 3 landmark answers, the fewest after which the lease can grant the role; lease_chances below completed means the hold is vacuous for the lease there
times the primary moved to the second landmark B1 (at most once per execution)
messages the switch thread dropped because of a failure, a cut or the attack (not the losses of the lossy sends)

param_columns.meaning: which controller code runs (--variant): nrp = NRPFD.rebeca, the backup has the shortcut (takes over at once when both networks go silent in the same round) and no lease; noopt = the shortcut removed, no lease; leasing = LeasingNRPFD.rebeca, no shortcut and the lease memory at the landmark

what breaks at the instants tA and tB (--fault): none; switch = DCN1's switch on that network dies and drops everything, the landmark included; link = DCN1's cable on that network is cut, DCN1's traffic is dropped but the switch and the landmark stay alive for DCN2
[0,-) = every heartbeat on both networks is dropped at the switch from tick 0 to the end of the run (--attack-from-ratio 0, no --attack-until-ratio); - = no attack (the binary prints [-,-))
--hb-on-nrp-change: off = the primary sends no heartbeat in the round in which it moves to the second landmark (NRPFD.rebeca); on = it does
ticks each controller handles (--rounds); the run ends at R*H (plus the phase offset)
the backup starts to worry when a network's count of rounds without news goes above this (--max-missed, default 2)
upper bound of one network hop (--u); every ratio flag is multiplied by U and rounded
lower bound of one network hop, round(--l-ratio * U), default L = U
storage lifetime: how long a message may wait at its receiver before it is handled, round(--sd-ratio * U), default 0; always 0 at the monitor
round length (heartbeat period), round(--h-ratio * U), default 20U
answer wait (ping timeout), round(--pt-ratio * U), default 10U
round(--phase-ratio * U): positive = DCN2 (the backup) starts its round timer that many ticks after DCN1; negative = DCN1 (the primary) starts that many ticks after DCN2; 0 = both tick together
instant at which network A fails (DCN1's switch A1, or DCN1's cable to it): round(--fail-a-ratio * U), default H + P; - when fault is none
instant at which network B fails: tA + sep; - when fault is none
round(--sep-ratio * U), default 0 (both networks fail together); negative = network B fails first. Derived: the binary prints tA and tB

boundary_law: Four rules, all from the header of the example (measured there on 2026-09-16, before every send became lossy; none is a published bound). (1) Case 7 with the backup's timer offset (regimes C1, C2, C3): a dual primary is reachable iff phase <= P or phase >= P + 4L, for 0 <= phase < H; v9 checks 9 points: L = U = 1: 10 violation, 11 and 13 safe, 14 violation; U = 2, L = 1: 20 violation, 21 and 23 safe, 24 violation; L = 0: 11 violation. (2) Two switch failures sep ticks apart, MARS node only (regimes E1, E2), J = U - L: over all failure instants a dual primary is reachable iff -(H + J) <= sep <= 2H + J without a heartbeat in the landmark-change round, and iff -(H + J) <= sep <= P + J with it; v9 checks 6 points at J = 0, each at the failure instant that witnesses the end: 40 violation, 41 safe, -20 violation, -21 safe; 10 violation, 11 safe. The violating set is not monotone in sep at a fixed tA and is not comparable with GulFest Eq. 5 / Eq. 6. (3) The lease is not enough (regimes F1, F2): with delta = -phase the lag of DCN1's timers, a dual primary is reachable iff 0 <= delta <= 3U - L; 9 points at L = U = 1 (phase +1 safe, 0, -1, -2 violation, -3 safe), from v9 where the run has finished and from v8 for the rest (state of 2026-10-11). (4) Case 8 with the lease (regime B): the lease holds because a primary question reaches the landmark before the backup's question of the same round whenever U < 3L; no cell crosses this bound. Every tested point agrees with its rule; the rules are not checked beyond these points in this campaign.

regimes.name: Self test: nothing fails and nobody attacks
regimes.params: variant nrp, fault none, no attack; U=1, L=1, sd=0, H=20, P=10, max=2, phase=0; R = 4 to 11
regimes.rule: No timing boundary is crossed: this is the self test of the harness (source header, 'Self test'). Variant nrp = the controller of NRPFD.rebeca, whose backup has the shortcut. Fault none = no switch dies and no cable is cut. With the clock every 'I am alive' note is sent at k*H + P and reaches the backup 4 hops (4 ticks) later, inside its own round of H = 20 ticks, so the backup's two counts never pass the patience limit and the backup never has to decide (the binary prints its vacuity warning: expected). A dual primary reported here would mean the harness loses messages. Without the clock a timer is only one more message: three backup ticks can pass before a heartbeat is delivered (source header, paragraph on the baseline with no failure), and the primary's answer wait can end before the landmark's answer is read (the v9 baseline rows count landmark changes and step-downs although nothing fails).
regimes.expect_timed: 0 violations and exactly 1 complete execution at every R; every other execution is blocked
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations: 34,707 (R=4), 253,953 (R=5), 1,559,235 (R=6), 8,872,170 (R=7) violating executions under keep-going; without keep-going (R=8, 10) the run stops at the first one in 0.02 s (exit 101)

regimes.name: Case 8 (attacker only), leasing variant, run too short for the lease to grant: R = 3 or 4
regimes.params: variant leasing, fault none, attack [0,-); U=1, L=1, sd=0, H=20, P=10, max=2, phase=0; R in {3, 4}
regimes.rule: Control, lease-vacuous. Variant leasing = the controller of LeasingNRPFD.rebeca (no shortcut; the backup takes over only after the landmark answered three of its questions in a row with no question of the primary in between). Fault none + attack [0,-) = nothing breaks, but every 'I am alive' note is dropped at the switch from tick 0 on; the landmark stays reachable and the primary is healthy. The lease needs 3 landmark answers to the backup (LEASE_MIN_ANSWERS = 3, source line 528) and the backup asks for the first time at its third tick, so only R - 2 takeover questions fit in the run: 1 at R = 3, 2 at R = 4. No execution, with or without the clock, can promote the backup (lease_chances = 0, the binary warns). These cells measure cost only.
regimes.expect_baseline: 0 violations as well: 320,909 complete executions at R = 3, 22,274,505 at R = 4

regimes.name: Case 8 (attacker only), leasing variant: the published Leasing NRP FD scenario, R = 5 and more
regimes.params: variant leasing, fault none, attack [0,-); U=1, L=1, sd=0, H=20, P=10, max=2, phase=0; R = 5 to 7
regimes.rule: MARS 2024 Table 1 case 8 with the leasing fix (the model of MARS Appendix C). Same variant, fault and attack as B-ctrl; from R = 5 three takeover questions fit in the run, so the lease could grant the role (lease_chances = completed, the hold is not vacuous). With the clock the primary's question reaches the landmark after 1 hop (at most U) and the backup's question of the same round after 3 hops (at least 3L); U < 3L, so a primary question precedes every backup question, every answer to the backup resets the lease (lease_resets = backup_replies) and the backup never takes over. Without the clock nothing orders the two questions at the landmark, so three answers in a row with no primary question in between are possible.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations; these cells run without keep-going, so the baseline stops at the first one (exit 101) after about 2 s (R = 5) and 7 s (R = 6)

regimes.name: Case 7 (both switches of DCN1 die together), backup's round timer offset inside the safe window, L = U = 1
regimes.params: variant nrp, fault switch, tA = tB = H + P = 30, no attack; U=1, L=1, sd=0, H=20, P=10, max=2; P < phase < P + 4L: phase 11 (R = 4 to 8) and 13 (R = 4)
regimes.rule: MARS 2024 Table 1 case 7 with the backup's timer shifted. Fault switch = the two switches DCN1 is plugged into (A1, which is the landmark, and B1) die at tA and tB and from then on drop everything, the backup's questions to the landmark included. Phase = DCN2 (the backup) starts its round timer that many ticks after DCN1. Source header: a dual primary is reachable iff phase <= P or phase >= P + 4L (0 <= phase < H). Here P + 1 = 11 <= phase <= P + 4L - 1 = 13: the backup's shortcut fires only after DCN1 has stepped down (promotions = stepdowns = completed = 2).
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations: 1,322,526 violating executions under keep-going at phase 11, R = 4 (v8; the v9 run has no row yet); without keep-going the run stops at the first one in under 0.01 s (exit 101)

regimes.name: Case 7, backup's round timer offset exactly on an end of the safe window, L = U = 1
regimes.params: as C1-safe, R = 4, with phase = P = 10 (lower end) or phase = P + 4L = 14 (upper end)
regimes.rule: Both ends of the window belong to the violating side (the rule is phase <= P or phase >= P + 4L). At phase = P the dual window [3H + phase, 3H + P] is the single instant 70 (a same-instant tie); at phase = P + 4L the heartbeat of round 0 can reach DCN2 exactly at its first tick, so DCN2 counts one round early.
regimes.expect_timed: a violation: the tool puts both ends on the violating side (run without keep-going: exit 101 after about 2 s, with a certified witness timeline)
regimes.expect_baseline: a violation (exit 101 at the first one, under 0.01 s)

regimes.name: Case 7, backup's round timer offset inside the safe window, jitter of one tick (U = 2, L = 1)
regimes.params: variant nrp, fault switch, tA = tB = H + P = 60, no attack; U=2, L=1, sd=0, H=40, P=20, max=2, R=4; P < phase < P + 4L: phase 21 and 23 (--phase-ratio 10.5 and 11.5)
regimes.rule: Same scenario and same rule as C1 with every ratio flag doubled by U = 2 and a transit that may take 1 or 2 ticks per hop: the safe window is P + 1 = 21 <= phase <= P + 4L - 1 = 23.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations (exit 101 at the first one, under 0.01 s)

regimes.name: Case 7, backup's round timer offset exactly on an end of the safe window, U = 2, L = 1
regimes.params: as C2-safe with phase = P = 20 (--phase-ratio 10) or phase = P + 4L = 24 (--phase-ratio 12)
regimes.rule: Both ends belong to the violating side, as in C1-edge.
regimes.expect_timed: a violation: the tool puts both ends on the violating side (exit 101 after about 2 s)
regimes.expect_baseline: a violation (exit 101 at the first one, under 0.01 s)

regimes.name: Case 7 with a transit that may take no time (U = 1, L = 0): the safe window is empty
regimes.params: variant nrp, fault switch, tA = tB = 30, no attack; U=1, L=0, sd=0, H=20, P=10, max=2, R=4; phase 11
regimes.rule: Same rule: phase <= P or phase >= P + 4L. With L = 0 the upper end P + 4L = 10 meets the lower end, so every phase is violating; phase 11, safe at L = 1, is one tick inside the violating side here (the cell name says 'edge moves with L').
regimes.expect_timed: a violation (run without keep-going: exit 101 after about 2 s)
regimes.expect_baseline: a violation (exit 101 at the first one, under 0.01 s)

regimes.name: Case 7 with the shortcut removed (variant noopt): the MARS Table 1 row
regimes.params: variant noopt, fault switch, tA = tB = H + P = 30, no attack; U=1, L=1, sd=0, H=20, P=10, max=2, phase=0, R=4
regimes.rule: No timing boundary in the cells that were run. Variant noopt = the nrp controller without the shortcut and without the lease (MARS 4.1, first step): the backup must ask the landmark before it takes over. Fault switch kills the landmark's switch, so with the clock no takeover question is ever answered (takeover_pings = 2, backup_replies = 0, promotions = 0) and DCN1 steps down in every execution (stepdowns = completed). Without the clock three backup ticks can pass before a heartbeat is delivered and a failure notice is one more message without an instant (source header: baseline noopt FIREs with the default switch failure at R = 4).
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations; run without keep-going: stops at the first one (exit 101) after about 18 s

regimes.name: Two switch failures some time apart, one tick outside the vulnerable window (no heartbeat in the landmark-change round)
regimes.params: variant nrp, fault switch, hb_on_change off, no attack; U=1, L=1 (J = U - L = 0), sd=0, H=20, P=10, max=2, phase=0; (tA, sep) = (11, 41) at R = 5 and (31, -21) at R = 4
regimes.rule: Network A's switch dies at tA and network B's at tB = tA + sep (sep < 0: B first). hb_on_change off = in the round in which the primary moves to the second landmark it sends no 'I am alive' note (NRPFD.rebeca). Source header, for the MARS node only: over all failure instants a dual primary is reachable iff -(H + J) <= sep <= 2H + J, here -20 <= sep <= 40. These cells sit one tick outside an end, at the failure instant tA that witnesses that end. Not comparable with GulFest Eq. 5 / Eq. 6 (that node also resets the count when it hears of a new landmark).
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations (exit 101 at the first one, under 0.01 s)

regimes.name: Two switch failures some time apart, exactly on an end of the vulnerable window (no heartbeat in the landmark-change round)
regimes.params: as E1-safe with (tA, sep) = (11, 40) at R = 5 (upper end 2H + J) and (31, -20) at R = 4 (lower end -(H + J))
regimes.rule: Both ends belong to the violating side (the rule is -(H + J) <= sep <= 2H + J). Each end is reached at one failure instant only (sep 40 at tA = 11, sep -20 at tA = 31, source header).
regimes.expect_timed: a violation: the tool puts both ends on the violating side (run without keep-going: exit 101 after about 86 s at (11, 40) and 20 s at (31, -20))
regimes.expect_baseline: a violation (exit 101 at the first one, under 0.01 s)

regimes.name: Two switch failures some time apart, one tick outside the vulnerable window (heartbeat also sent in the landmark-change round)
regimes.params: variant nrp, fault switch, hb_on_change on, no attack; U=1, L=1 (J = 0), sd=0, H=20, P=10, max=2, phase=0, R=4; (tA, sep) = (1, 11)
regimes.rule: hb_on_change on = the primary sends its 'I am alive' notes also in the round in which it moves to the second landmark (the change GulFest describes for its modified implementation, applied here to the MARS node). Source header: dual primary reachable iff -(H + J) <= sep <= P + J, here -20 <= sep <= 10; the cell is one tick above the upper end. Only the upper end is probed in this campaign.
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations (exit 101 at the first one, under 0.01 s)

regimes.name: Two switch failures some time apart, exactly on the upper end of the vulnerable window (heartbeat also sent in the landmark-change round)
regimes.params: as E2-safe with (tA, sep) = (1, 10): sep = P + J
regimes.rule: The end belongs to the violating side (sep <= P + J); it is reached at tA = 1 only (source header).
regimes.expect_timed: a violation: the tool puts the end on the violating side (run without keep-going: exit 101 after about 0.4 s)
regimes.expect_baseline: a violation (exit 101 at the first one, under 0.01 s)

regimes.name: The lease is not enough: DCN1's two uplinks cut while the heartbeats are wiped out; timers one tick outside the vulnerable window (patience limit 2)
regimes.params: variant leasing, fault link, tA = tB = 50, attack [0,-); U=1, L=1, sd=0, H=20, P=10, max=2, R=5; phase +1 (delta = -1) and phase -3 (delta = 3)
regimes.rule: New scenario of this example (not in the papers, not cross-checked in Afra). Fault link = at tA and tB the two cables of DCN1 are cut: DCN1's traffic is dropped, but the switches and the landmark stay alive and keep answering the backup. Attack [0,-) wipes out every heartbeat from tick 0. Phase < 0 = DCN1 starts its round timer |phase| ticks after DCN2; delta = -phase is how far DCN1's timers lag the backup's. The lease grants the role after two rounds without a primary question, which is exactly the primary's own give-up time. Source header: dual primary iff 0 <= delta <= 3U - L, here 0 <= delta <= 2 (phase 0, -1, -2). At phase +1 the backup promotes one tick after the step-down; at phase -3 one more primary question reaches the landmark and resets the lease.
regimes.expect_timed: 0 violations, 2 complete executions, stepdowns = lease_chances = completed (not vacuous)
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations (exit 101 at the first one, about 0.3 s)

regimes.name: The lease is not enough: timers exactly on an end of the vulnerable window (patience limit 2)
regimes.params: as F1-safe with phase 0 (delta = 0) or phase -2 (delta = 3U - L = 2)
regimes.rule: Both ends belong to the violating side (0 <= delta <= 3U - L). At delta = 0 the backup promotes at 90, the very instant DCN1 steps down (a same-instant tie, explored in both orders).
regimes.expect_timed: a violation: the tool puts both ends on the violating side (run without keep-going: exit 101 after about 27 min at phase 0; phase -2 took 87 min in v8)
regimes.expect_baseline: a violation (exit 101 at the first one, about 0.3 s)

regimes.name: The lease is not enough, same scenario one round earlier (patience limit 1); timers one tick outside the vulnerable window
regimes.params: variant leasing, fault link, tA = tB = 30, attack [0,-); U=1, L=1, sd=0, H=20, P=10, max=1, R=4; phase +1 and phase -3
regimes.rule: The F1 scenario translated by one round: with max = 1 the backup worries one round earlier, so the cut is at 30 instead of 50 and R = 4 instead of 5 (the dual instant moves from 90 to 70). These cells are not in the source header: they were derived by hand for the v8 plan, and the measured verdicts follow the same rule 0 <= delta <= 3U - L = 2.
regimes.expect_timed: 0 violations, 2 complete executions (v8; the v9 runs have no row yet)
regimes.expect_baseline: spurious violations (exit 101 at the first one, about 0.3 s)

regimes.name: The lease is not enough, one round earlier (patience limit 1); timers exactly on an end of the vulnerable window
regimes.params: as F2-safe with phase 0 (delta = 0) or phase -2 (delta = 3U - L = 2)
regimes.rule: Both ends belong to the violating side, as in F1-edge.
regimes.expect_timed: a violation: the tool puts both ends on the violating side (run without keep-going: exit 101 after about 11 min at phase 0 and 20 min at phase -2)
regimes.expect_baseline: a violation (exit 101 at the first one, about 0.3 s)

regimes.name: The lease is not enough, one round earlier (patience limit 1); timers inside the vulnerable window
regimes.rule: 0 < delta < 3U - L: strictly inside the window, both controllers are in charge for a strict interval, not only at one instant.
regimes.expect_timed: a violation (run without keep-going: exit 101 after about 11 min)
regimes.expect_baseline: a violation (exit 101 at the first one, about 0.3 s)

glossary.meaning: the two controllers (distributed controller nodes). DCN1 starts as the primary (in charge), DCN2 as the backup
both controllers in charge at the same instant: the violation this example looks for
the network reference point: the switch the primary uses as a landmark, A1 at the start, B1 after a change. Only a controller that still reaches the landmark may be in charge

two separate networks join the controllers, each a chain of three switches (A1, A2, A3 and B1, B2, B3). DCN1 is plugged into A1 and B1, DCN2 into A3 and B3. One thread (SW) plays A1 and B1; the other switches are folded into transit
one switch-to-switch or node-to-switch step, between L and U ticks. DCN1 to its switch is 1 hop, the switch to DCN2 is 3 hops, a heartbeat travels 4 hops
the 'I am alive' note the primary sends to the backup on each network every round, at the end of its answer wait and only if the landmark answered
the 'are you there?' question a controller sends to the landmark. A takeover ping is the backup's question sent because both networks have gone silent
the heartbeat period: both controllers wake up once per round
the ping timeout: how long a controller waits for the landmark's answer
the backup keeps one count of rounds without news per network and starts to worry when a count goes above max (default 2: on the third silent round)
variant nrp only: when both counts go over the limit in the same round the backup takes over at once, without asking the landmark

variant leasing only: with every answer the landmark says whether the question before came from the primary; the backup takes over only after three answers in a row with no primary question in between
a hold in which the lease could never have granted the role (fewer than 3 landmark answers to the backup: lease_chances below completed), so it is no evidence for the lease
DCN1 gives up being primary after neither landmark answered; it never returns in this model
DCN2 takes over as primary

rows of MARS 2024 Table 1. Case 7: both switches of DCN1 fail at the same instant H + P. Case 8: something wipes out the heartbeats while the landmark stays reachable (here an attack window at the switch)
the offset between the two round timers (see the Phase column); delta = -phase is how many ticks DCN1's timers lag DCN2's
jitter of one hop, U - L
--promote-rule: takeover (default, ETFA Algorithm 3: only an answered takeover ping promotes) or any (the MARS node verbatim: any answered ping promotes). Every v9 cell runs takeover

every message carries a sequence number and every receive assumes the expected one; every channel ends with a Done message. An execution in which a message was lost, or skipped by a later one, blocks instead of acting on a silence that never happened. It is scaffolding, not protocol

executions stopped by the harness guard (a lost or skipped message) plus, under keep-going, the violating executions. Almost every explored execution is blocked: a completed execution is one without any loss
a line the binary prints after a hold in which the scenario did not bite (the backup never had to decide, DCN1 was not fully isolated, or the lease was never consulted)
the timed side prints, with a violation, an assignment of instants to every event of the violating execution
the controller code of the MARS 2024 Rebeca files (modelled here) and of the Gul Agha Festschrift timing-analysis file (not modelled: it also resets a count when it hears of a new landmark)
the example's own words: FIRE = the run found a dual primary (exit code 101 when it runs without keep-going); hold = the run explored everything and found none (exit code 0)

kg = run with --keep-going: the search goes on after a violation, explores everything and counts every violating execution (exhaustive). no-kg = run without it: the run stops at the first certified violation with exit code 101 (first-violation); a side that meets no violation still explores everything
M = the patience limit max; cut = the instant tA = tB at which both cables of DCN1 are cut

header cell = the lease-not-enough scenario exactly as written in the header of the source file (max 2, cut at 50, R = 5); translated = the same scenario moved one round earlier by max 1 (cut at 30, R = 4)
the value of the column 'Heartbeat on landmark change'
the Leasing NRP FD model printed in MARS 2024 Appendix C: attacker only, no switch failure

With every send lossy, a lost message always blocks the execution at the harness guard (sequence gap or a Done that never comes), so the completed executions are exactly the loss-free ones: the model checked is the reliable-channel model of the Rebeca files, and message loss adds cost only. Whether to keep the guard under universal loss is an open modelling decision.
Under keep-going a violating execution is counted in blocked, not in execs (the assertion aborts it): explored = execs + blocked already contains the violating executions.
